methodologyNotes: Covers handheld hiking and trekking poles sold at a published US MSRP, spanning telescoping, folding (z-fold), and fixed-length shafts. Excludes ski/alpine touring poles without a hiking basket, walking canes, and monopods. Price is typical US retail in USD for a PAIR (two poles), the standard purchase unit. shaftMaterial is the primary shaft construction as an enum: carbon-fiber, aluminum-7075, aluminum-6061, or carbon-aluminum-hybrid. weightPerPoleGrams is manufacturer-published weight of a SINGLE pole in grams, excluding baskets, at the shortest configuration. packedLengthCm is the collapsed (telescoping) or folded (z-fold) length in cm; for fixed poles it equals the fixed length. minLengthCm and maxLengthCm are the usable length range in cm; for fixed-length poles min equals max. sections is the integer count of shaft segments. foldMechanism is an enum: telescoping, z-fold, or fixed. lockMechanism is an enum: lever-lock, twist-lock, push-button, or none. gripMaterial is an enum: cork, eva-foam, rubber, or cork-blend. adjustable is a boolean (true if usable length is user-adjustable). antiShock is a boolean (true if an internal shock-absorbing spring is fitted). null means the manufacturer does not disclose the value.

products.name: MSR Dynalock Ascent Carbon
products.priceNote: US MSRP $190 for the pair. Treeline Review (Jan 21, 2025) states "Price: $190" and its comparison table lists "MSRP $190"; Better Trail (Jan 20, 2025) lists "MSR DynaLock Ascent Carbon ($190)". MSR's own regional store page displayed no USD price (EU region, EUR 0,00).
products.provenance: The MSR/Cascade Designs official product page confirms the exact model "DynaLock Ascent Carbon Backcountry Poles" (SKUs 10236/10237), listing Kevlar-reinforced carbon-fiber construction, an EVA foam grip, and 20 cm of tool-free DynaLock adjustment via an anodized aluminum lever, with two size SKUs (Small 100-120 cm / Large 120-140 cm); because length, packed length and weight differ by size and MSR publishes weight only per pair (0.47/0.50 kg), those size-dependent numeric fields are left null. The dated Treeline Review (Jan 21, 2025) corroborates the same model and construction, describes the tri-fold three-piece folding design with a single lever-lock length adjustment, and states the US price verbatim as "Price: $190" and "MSRP $190". Better Trail (Jan 20, 2025) independently lists the pole at $190 with "Type: Folding/telescoping", "Grip Material: Foam" and a "metal lever lock", confirming both identity and price.

products.name: Black Diamond Alpine Carbon Cork

products.provenance: The Black Diamond official product page confirms this exact model — "Alpine Carbon Cork Trekking Poles" (Tundra, #BD1125143010ALL1) — with SPECS: Weight 486 g, Size Range/Usable Length 100-130 cm, Collapsed Length 61 cm, 100% carbon fiber shafts, 100% natural cork grip, and FlickLock Pro adjustability, at Regular price $229.95 USD. The CleverHiker review (dated June 16, 2025) corroborates the same model at $230 with Shaft Material Carbon Fiber, Grip Material Cork, Collapsed Length 24 in, a "telescoping design" with "flick-lock," and a stated Weight (Pair) of 1 lb 1.1 oz — confirming BD's 486 g figure is per pair, so no single-pole weight is disclosed. weightPerPoleGrams and sections are left null because neither fetched page states a single-pole gram weight or an explicit integer section count verbatim.

products.name: Black Diamond Distance Carbon Z
products.priceNote: US MSRP $219.95 USD for the pair (two poles), from the Black Diamond official product page ("Regular price $219.95 USD", SKU #BD11255440071101), accessed 2026-07-13. Retailer corroboration (The Trail Runner Store) is a Canadian shop priced in CAD, so not used for the USD figure.
products.provenance: The Black Diamond official product page (SKU #BD11255440071101) confirms this exact model — "The Distance Carbon Z is our lightest Z-Pole with 100% carbon construction" — at a US MSRP of $219.95 USD for the pair, with 100% carbon fiber shafts, a lightweight EVA foam grip, three-section Z-pole "fixed length construction" (non-adjustable), and usable lengths of 105, 110, 115, 120, 125, and 130 cm. The Trail Runner Store retailer page corroborates the identical model and spec table but explicitly labels the weight column "Weight (Per Pair)" (105 cm = 256 g … 130 cm = 296 g), confirming Black Diamond discloses only PER-PAIR weight — so weightPerPoleGrams is left null rather than guessed, and packedLengthCm is null because the collapsed length varies by size (35–44 cm) with no single disclosed value. The retailer also documents the "single push-button release" Speed Cone deployment (supporting lockMechanism = push-button), and neither page lists any internal shock-absorbing spring, so antiShock = false.

products.name: Leki Makalu FX Carbon
products.priceNote: US MSRP $229.95 listed verbatim on the LEKI USA official product page (lekiusa.com/products/makalu-fx-carbon, SKU 65620622C: "$229.95 USD"). Corroborated at $230 (rounded) in The Big Outside review dated July 2026 ("$230, 1 lb. 1.9 oz./508g (per pair)"). Price is for a pair (Unit: Pair).
products.provenance: The LEKI USA official product page (SKU 65620622C, "MAKALU FX CARBON") confirms the exact model and lists a full spec sheet used verbatim: Shaft Material Carbon (PRC 1000) -> carbon-fiber; standard Weight per pole 252 g; Pack Size 41 cm; Sizerun 110-130 cm (standard); Number of segments 5 (Standard); Folding System ELD with SpeedLock 2 Plus lever Locking System; Aergon Air EVA-foam grip; and US MSRP $229.95. The Big Outside review (dated July 2026) corroborates model identity as the folding, one-size 110-130 cm Makalu FX Carbon at $230 with "Aergon Air foam grips" and "Speedlock 2 Plus lever locks," distinguishing it from the AS (anti-shock), Pro, and FX.One siblings. Where the two sources conflict, the manufacturer figures were used (pack size 41 cm vs the review's 40 cm; 5 segments vs the review's "three-section" phrasing); antiShock is false because LEKI sells a separate "Makalu FX Carbon AS" anti-shock model and no shock spring is listed for this base version.

products.name: Leki Legacy Lite
products.priceNote: LEKI USA official product page lists the LEGACY LITE (SKU 65621841S) at "$109.95 USD". Price is per pair (Unit: Pair). Campmor lists the same model but showed it sold out with no readable price, so the figure is taken from the manufacturer page.
products.provenance: The LEKI USA manufacturer page (SKU 65621841S) confirmed the exact LEGACY LITE model and listed the price "$109.95 USD" plus a full spec table: Weight per pole 251 g, Pack Size 66 cm, 3 segments, Speed Lock plus locking system, EVOCON CorTec grip (80% natural cork combined with soft material), Aluminum (HTS 6.0) shaft, and a carbide Flex Tip, adjustable 100-135 cm. Campmor corroborated the identical spec sheet under the same base SKU (65621841) — matching Pack Size 66 cm, 251 g/pole, 3 segments, Speed Lock plus, EVOCON grip, and HTS 6.0 aluminum — confirming this is the standard LEGACY LITE (non-AS, no anti-shock spring), not the anti-shock or a sibling variant. Campmor's price field errored out (item sold out), so the price is sourced solely from the manufacturer page. shaftMaterial was left null because the pages state only "Aluminum (HTS 6.0)", which does not verbatim match the allowed 6061/7075 enum values.

products.name: Cascade Mountain Tech Carbon Fiber Quick Lock
products.priceNote: Cascade Mountain Tech official product page lists "Regular price $64.99" for the "Carbon Fiber Quick Lock Trekking Poles (Cork Grip) - Black" (variant price field 6499). Per methodology this is the price for a PAIR (two poles), which is how Cascade sells this SKU.
products.provenance: The Cascade Mountain Tech official product page confirmed this exact model — "Carbon Fiber Quick Lock Trekking Poles (Cork Grip)" at a Regular price of $64.99 (a pair) — with a Features list stating verbatim: Shaft Material 100% Carbon Fiber, Grip Material Cork, Locking Mechanism Quick Lock, three named sections (Upper/Middle/Lower), single-pole weight 8.1 oz, and lengths 26" collapsed / 54" extended. Weight and lengths are published only in ounces/inches for this exact model, so the grams/cm spec fields are left null rather than converted, and no release date is disclosed.

products.name: Retrospec Solstice

Backpacker's June 2026 roundup separately shows "$30 at Retrospec" and a "$25" figure in its comparison chart. Using the manufacturer's stated $29.99 pair MSRP.

Per-pole weight in grams is not disclosed (the manufacturer lists only a 640g pair weight; Backpacker lists "11.3 oz" per pole), grip material is a buyer-selectable foam-or-cork choice, and anti-shock is not stated, so those keys are left null.
